title: Gilgamesh and Enkidu
text:
Gilgamesh, king of Uruk, was two parts god and one part man, and he was a tyrant. He wore out the young men of the city and took what he wanted, and the people cried out to the gods. So the gods made a match for him: Enkidu, a wild man who lived among the animals on the steppe. Through the woman Shamhat, Enkidu learned to eat bread, drink beer and live among people, and he came to Uruk.

When Gilgamesh came to enter a wedding house, Enkidu blocked the door with his foot. The two grappled like bulls, smashing the doorposts and shaking the walls. At last Gilgamesh threw him, and as his anger cooled, the two became the closest of friends.

Together they went to the Cedar Forest and killed its guardian Humbaba, and back in Uruk they slew the Bull of Heaven. But the gods decreed that one of them must die for these deeds, and it was Enkidu. He fell ill and died after twelve days.

Gilgamesh refused to let him be buried. He wept over him for seven days and seven nights, until a worm fell from his friend's nose. Then, terrified of death, he put on a lion skin and wandered the wilderness, searching for a way to live forever.
lesson: A real friend can turn rivalry into partnership and change who you are. Value such people while they are with you, because their loss reshapes your life.
source: Epic of Gilgamesh, Standard Babylonian version, Tablets I to X
